properties.answer:
Yes — build it. Anthony, 2026-08-07, after asking for the question in plain English and a recommendation. This is the second "yes": the 2026-08-06 one un-deferred the requirement, and this one answers the precondition that requirement carried — whether the kit may report its own ADOPTION without breaking dec:loop-status-state-not-history.

Settled as dec:adoption-is-reported-the-loop-still-computes (accepted): the distinction is REAL, because that decision protects one specific thing — the answer to "what does this design still need?" must not depend on who did what — and adoption never touches that answer. It is a different question (is the TOOL being used as intended?), for a different reader (the maintainer), changing a different thing (the tool). The line is held by three properties rather than a promise: the count lives in session state and offline transcripts, never in the graph; no adoption field is read by loop_status / detect_gaps / detect_defects; and a check asserts the loop's answer is unchanged whether or not the count exists. The standing test for anything added later: does this measurement ever change what the loop says is owed? If yes, it is forbidden whatever it is called.

Built as cap:skill-loads-are-counted. Deliberately smaller than the requirement's title, and the gap between the two is stated rather than glossed: this measures LOADING, not FOLLOWING. The offline half already existed (tools/surface_usage.py, which has counted get_skill calls since 2026-08-01 and writes nothing to any graph); the missing half was near-real-time, and it is the hole chg:undefer-skill-adherence-measurement named — every shape cap:skill-triggers recognises lives in the graph-write stream, and "no skill has been loaded" is not a graph write.

Recommendation he accepted, recorded because the ordering was a judgement and not an obvious one: fix the trigger first (it attacks the actual complaint, which was having to remind agents by hand), then the reporting. Stated to him at the time: an agent recommending that the tool nudge agents rather than measure them has an interest in that ordering, and he should weight it accordingly.
properties.context_setter: Nothing satisfies requirement “Whether the kit is actually used is measured, not inferred from whether the design looks tidy”
properties.question: Right now there is no way to tell whether anyone's agent is actually using reflow2's skills — a project can look perfectly healthy while the kit is barely being touched. Do you want reflow2 to measure that, knowing it sits close to a rule you set about not reasoning from what an agent did in past runs?
